newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani ports need modernisation - UK mission.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani ports need modernisation - UK mission.

text.p: Pakistani ports need considerable modernisation, the leader of a British ports mission said at the end of a six-day visit.
The mission visited Karachi Port and nearby Port Qasim and discussed future plans with port and government officials.
"I think both sides have recognised there is a need for considerable modernisation," mission leader Henry Rowe told a news conference.

Modernisation is needed for bulk cargo, containerisation and special terminals for grain handling, Rowe said. There was also a need to improve productivity and his team had identified projects and discussed them with those promoting them.
Rowe said the proposed new port at Gwadar could be developed to cater for the needs of the Central Asian states.
Pakistani officials say seaborne trade forecast by the year 2000 is 42 million tonnes and projections for 2005, 2010 and 2015 are 53, 71 and 92 million tonnes respectively.
